clue.text: When abroad, use phone with nothing in memory

indicators.note: in tells us the zero for nothing sits within the word for memory

parts.note: RAM is random-access memory in a computer or phone
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: Advice about running up phone bills overseas with an empty phone memory.
explanation.definitionFit: Roaming is the term for a mobile connecting through a foreign network while travelling.

clue.text: Transport similar to mass gathering?

definitions.meaning: punning 'rave-ish', like a rave, a large dance party

explanation.surface: Getting carried away, like being at a huge crowd event.
explanation.definitionFit: Ravish means fill with delight; the second reading treats it as rave plus -ish suffix.

clue.text: Wasted and full of oneself — no use whatever

parts.note: all in means exhausted, wasted
vain means conceited, full of oneself

explanation.surface: A drunk and self-absorbed person proves utterly useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wasted' suggests drunk; here it means worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Done all in vain means done with no result or benefit whatever.

clue.text: Extremely tedious, going down to get water

definitions.meaning: drilling a well down to the water table

explanation.surface: Someone complains that digging for water is dreary work.
explanation.definitionFit: Colloquial British 'well' means very, while boring a well means drilling a shaft for water.

clue.text: Old footballer chucking last boot out

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: chucking last means the final letter of the footballer's name is thrown away

parts.note: Pele was the great Brazilian footballer

explanation.surface: A retired football star throws out his last boot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boot' looks like footwear in the football picture; 'boot out' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To expel is to throw someone out, to eject or dismiss them.

clue.text: Seal savaged fish keeping its head down — ray?

indicators.note: savaged suggests mauled into pieces, so the letters of Seal are rearranged
the fish's first letter is moved lower down the word

parts.note: bream is a fish

explanation.surface: A seal mauls a fish lying low, perhaps a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'savaged' turns SEAL into LASE; moving B of BREAM down a place gives RBEAM. 'ray' looks like the fish but is a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser beam is a concentrated ray of light, so a ray is an example.

clue.text: Excessive ego of one pursuing maiden?

definitions.text: Excessive ego of one pursuing maiden?

parts.words: Excessive ego of one pursuing maiden?
parts.note: a suitor's cockiness, or in cricket a bowler going for a maiden over, an over with no runs

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a maiden is an over without a run conceded, so the answer splits as OVER + CONFIDENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Overconfidence is excessive self-assurance, the cockiness of someone too sure of success.

clue.text: Fool regularly taking Air Djibouti

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the second, fourth and so on

explanation.surface: A fool books a flight with an African airline.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiot is a stupid person, a fool.

clue.text: Leaves fish out of water, might one suppose?

parts.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
a fish out of water is on land

explanation.surface: A fish departing the water, one might imagine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaves' looks like a verb; it is the noun, a wreath of foliage.
explanation.definitionFit: A garland is a wreath of flowers and leaves.

clue.text: Pub obtaining means of digital identification as business asset?

parts.note: a bar is a pub
gaining means obtaining
a microchip identifies pets, cards and passports electronically

explanation.surface: A bar acquires a chip system as a company asset.
explanation.definitionFit: A bargaining chip is something held for use as leverage in negotiations.

clue.text: Very sick beginning to 'Animal House'

parts.note: ill means sick

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter, here of Animal

explanation.surface: A film review: the start of the comedy Animal House is truly nauseating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal House' reads as the film title, but House is the definition and only Animal's first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A villa is a large country or suburban residence.

clue.text: Advert around carnival city showing butt

indicators.note: around says the advert word wraps itself about the city's name

parts.note: a poster is a printed advertisement
Rio de Janeiro is famous for its carnival

explanation.surface: A billboard ad for Rio's carnival features a prominent bottom.
explanation.definitionFit: Posterior is a jocular word for the backside, as is butt in American English.

clue.text: Eagles flying over North African country

indicators.note: the shuffled birds are spread over, covering, the abbreviation for North
flying birds scatter, so the letters of Eagles are rearranged

parts.note: N is the compass abbreviation for North

explanation.surface: Birds of prey wheel above a country in the north of Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North African country' looks like one definition, but North supplies N, and Senegal is in West Africa anyway.
explanation.definitionFit: Senegal is a nation on the Atlantic coast of West Africa.

clue.text: Italians make a meal of this reform of Riot Act

definitions.text: Italians make a meal of this

indicators.note: to reform something is to reshape it, so the letters of Riot Act are rearranged

explanation.surface: Italians fuss over the Riot Act being rewritten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'make a meal of' suggests overdoing a fuss, but here it is literal: Italians eat it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ricotta is a soft Italian whey cheese used in many dishes.

clue.text: Royal adviser on radio raised stakes

indicators.note: a radio broadcast is heard, not seen, so the phrase is replaced by a word sounding the same

parts.note: a royal residence is a palace; an aide is an adviser or assistant

explanation.surface: A courtier appears on the airwaves and ups the ante.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised stakes' reads as upping a bet; it is a fence of upright stakes.
explanation.definitionFit: A palisade is a defensive fence made of pointed wooden posts set upright.

clue.text: Breaking rule with date, right? I am

definitions.text: Breaking rule with date, right? I am

indicators.note: breaking scatters the letters of the two words, as a rule is broken

explanation.surface: A cheat confesses: I broke the rule by going on a date.
explanation.walkthrough: As &lit, the whole clue is the speaker's admission: someone who breaks the marriage rule with a date.
explanation.definitionFit: An adulterer is a married person unfaithful to their spouse, breaking the marital rule.

clue.text: After rejection, half-hearted offspring proceeded cautiously

indicators.note: After puts the trimmed offspring word behind the refusal

parts.note: no is a rejection

indicators.note: the heart of the word for offspring is a double letter, and losing half of it leaves one

parts.note: seed means offspring, as in biblical use

explanation.surface: After being turned down, an unenthusiastic child crept forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-hearted' removes one of the two middle E's of SEED, leaving SED.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose forward is to move slowly and carefully, like a vehicle edging out.

clue.text: Two options for gambler to make pair out of singleton?

definitions.meaning: in poker one may see (match) a bet or double it

definitions.text: to make pair out of singleton?
definitions.meaning: seeing double is perceiving two of a single thing

explanation.surface: A gambler's choices for turning one card into two.
explanation.definitionFit: See and double are both betting calls, and seeing double is blurred twin vision.

clue.text: Territory taken back in Egyptianisation

indicators.note: taken back says those letters are read from right to left
in shows the letters sit inside the long word Egyptianisation

explanation.surface: Land recovered during Egypt's drive to make things Egyptian.
explanation.walkthrough: Inside EgyptIANISation is IANIS, which read backwards gives the answer; aptly, Egypt took Sinai back from Israel.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinai is the peninsula and region between Egypt and Israel.

clue.text: New player joining team in collapse

parts.note: a sub, substitute, is a new player brought on
a side is a team

explanation.surface: A team folds just as a substitute comes on.
explanation.definitionFit: To subside is to sink or cave in, as ground does.

clue.text: Cropped male nude I sent — not in post

indicators.note: sent, as in sent flying, signals the letters are scattered
a cropped word has its tail cut off

parts.note: taken as written before trimming

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to sending a trimmed nude selfie, though not by mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cropped' cuts nude to NUD; 'sent' shuffles MALE + NUD + I.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unmailed has never been dispatched through the postal service.

clue.text: Punk, notwithstanding trousers, to get out of bondage

indicators.note: trousers as a verb means pockets, so the words hold the answer inside them

explanation.surface: A punk in bondage trousers manages to escape them.
explanation.walkthrough: Bondage trousers were a strapped punk fashion; 'trousers' is a verb meaning pockets.
explanation.definitionFit: To unknot is to untie, freeing something bound by knots.

clue.text: Snap up building land on basis of report and from appearance

indicators.note: a report is something heard, so the phrase gives a word that sounds alike

parts.note: to snap up is to buy; a plot for building is a site

explanation.surface: A property developer buys a plot after reading a survey and seeing it.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing someone by sight means recognising them by how they look.

clue.text: Made light of American replacing English language in Africa

indicators.note: replacing means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: shone means gave off light

explanation.surface: An American trivialised English when it supplanted an African tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made light of' suggests belittling; 'of' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shona is a Bantu language spoken mainly in Zimbabwe.

clue.text: 'A Song for Europe'? Have to go to bed!

parts.note: a Lied is a German art song, so a song for (a European in) Europe
to own is to have

explanation.surface: Someone sick of the old Eurovision selection show is told to turn in.
explanation.walkthrough: A Song for Europe was the UK's TV contest picking its Eurovision entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying down is taking to bed to rest or sleep.

clue.text: Composer, unknown, dropping down ranks of minor celebrity

indicators.note: dropping down means the unknown letter moves further down the word

parts.note: the Z-list is the lowest tier of celebrity
z is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An obscure composer slides down the minor-celebrity rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving Z of ZLIST down three places gives LISZT.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and pianist.

clue.text: Hotlines, perhaps, between ideologies being different

indicators.note: between puts the word for different between the halves of the ideologies word

parts.note: isms are ideologies or doctrines
other means different

explanation.surface: Emergency phone links between rival political systems, Cold War style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hotlines' suggests the Moscow-Washington phone line; it is lines joining hot places on a weather map.
explanation.definitionFit: Isotherms are map lines joining points of equal temperature, so a hot one is an example.

clue.text: Metal bar from island

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper, a metal
to bar is to ban

explanation.surface: An iron bar made from ore found on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuban describes a person or thing originating in Cuba, a Caribbean island nation.

clue.text: Anger old queen — snake, being clasped, bit

indicators.note: being clasped means the snake is held between the parts around it

parts.note: ex means former or old
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is a queen
an asp is a snake
ate is the past tense of eat, as bit is of bite

explanation.surface: A former queen, Cleopatra-like, is bitten by a clutched snake and is angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bit' looks like the snake's bite in the Cleopatra picture, but it is a past tense supplying the final piece; 'being clasped' puts the snake inside the old queen pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To exasperate is to irritate or infuriate someone intensely.

clue.text: Message from old flame in 'Times'

indicators.note: in tells us the former lover sits within the two letters for Times

parts.note: T stands for time, so two make times
an ex is a former partner

explanation.surface: A personal ad from a former lover appears in The Times newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A text is a short written message sent by phone.
